name: Chili Lime Chicken Burrito
writer_notes: STAGE2: built from burrito-stage1-builds C9. The source is a TikTok video; its caption macros were NOT used. These numbers are built from ingredients in stage 1. Credit the source, but the numbers are ours.
The sauce is the Greek-yogurt variant the source offers (yogurt plus hot sauce), not the mayo version.

DROPPED: stage 1 listed 9 g of shredded lettuce as a cold garnish. Lettuce has NO row in either the food-macros-db or db/ingredients.json, and raw lettuce wilts badly in a reheated meal-prep burrito, so it is left out rather than invented. Its calorie impact was under 2 cal per serving, inside the macro tolerance. FLAG for the repair pass: either confirm the drop or have the mapper add a Lettuce/Romaine row.
Differs from the live Slow Cooker Cilantro Lime Chicken Bowls by being a chili-lime seared breast with a spicy yogurt drizzle in a wrap; the selector notes this is the softest TikTok keep.
Fresh tomato is mapped to Cherry Tomatoes (fresh) since the DB carries no plain fresh tomato row.
intro_html: Chili and lime is the two ingredient handshake that makes cheap chicken taste like a taqueria. We rub breast with chili powder, lime and salt, sear it hard, and drizzle on a spicy Greek yogurt sauce, then load in fresh tomato and red onion for crunch and a little melty mozzarella to hold it together. Every burrito comes in under 400 calories with 4 ounces of meat and {{protein}} grams of protein, on a high fiber tortilla that keeps you near 5 grams of net carb. We have Slow Cooker Cilantro Lime Chicken Bowls on the site; this is the faster, spicier, hand-held take, seared instead of slow cooked and finished with a hot yogurt drizzle.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1582 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb: ~$7.78. Buy 4 lbs: $8.92.
Pantry seasonings (chili powder, salt): ~$0.20. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $29.94 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.14 per burrito. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $36.98 across 14 servings, roughly $2.64 per burrito. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $13.95 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $50.93. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a burrito (at everyday cost) for chili lime chicken that costs a rub and a squeeze. The yogurt and hot sauce do the work a bottle of dressing usually charges you for.
shop_smart: Chili powder is cheapest in the bulk container, and a burrito batch this size uses a real spoonful, so the small jar will not cut it.
Limes are cheapest by the bag, and you want the juice fresh here, so buy a handful and roll them hard before you squeeze.
Greek yogurt plus hot sauce is the whole sauce, no mayo required. Buy the big tub of yogurt since it shows up all over this batch.
Chicken breast in the family pack is the best value. Cook what this batch needs and freeze the rest.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rub the chicken breast with the chili powder, lime juice, salt and olive oil.
Sear the chicken in a hot pan until charred at the edges and cooked through, then slice or chop it.
Stir the hot sauce into the Greek yogurt to make the spicy drizzle.
Dice the tomato and red onion for the fresh topping.
Lay chopped chicken down each tortilla, add a share of tomato and onion, a scatter of reduced fat mozzarella and a spoon of the spicy yogurt.
Weigh the chicken, tomato and onion together, subtract the empty bowl, and divide by 14 so each burrito is even, then fold in the sides and roll.
Wrap each burrito and portion into 14 containers.
portion_html: Weigh the chicken and the fresh vegetables, subtract the empty bowl, and divide by 14, then sauce, cheese and roll each tortilla to match. Each burrito carries {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. If you are freezing these, keep the yogurt drizzle in a side cup and add it after reheating.
